chapters.title: Chapter 5: Comparing Markets Like an Investor

lessons.title: Your Global Morning Dashboard: What to Check Before NSE Opens

children.text: Think back to Tuesday, 15 September 2026. The Nifty fell 1.19% to a five-month low, the rupee slid to 95.92, and IT stocks rose while realty and metals fell. None of that was a surprise to an investor who spent 15 minutes that morning checking Brent crude near $108, US bond yields near 5%, a stronger dollar, a week of FPI selling and a Fed decision due within 48 hours. You have now learned how the US, Europe and Asia work, how to compare their valuations and how global shocks travel to the Nifty. This final lesson turns all of it into a simple routine you can run every trading morning before NSE opens.

body.text: Fifteen minutes, ten numbers, checked in the order the world wakes up. The goal is not to predict every tick of the Nifty. It is to walk into the trading day knowing what has already happened, so that nothing that happens next feels random.

body.title: A global morning routine, IST (US and Europe on daylight saving time)

events.title: Wall Street closes
events.description: The S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Dow set their closing levels. Check them when you wake up, not at 1:30 am.

events.title: Tokyo and Seoul open
events.description: The Nikkei 225, TOPIX and KOSPI give Asia's first reaction to the US session.

events.title: GIFT Nifty, Taiwan and Singapore open
events.description: GIFT Nifty's morning session starts, and the TAIEX signals the mood in chip stocks.

events.title: Hong Kong and Shanghai open
events.description: China-related news and Chinese data, usually released around 7:30 am IST, get priced in.

events.title: Your 15-minute dashboard
events.description: The ideal window: most of Asia is trading, GIFT Nifty is active and overnight news is available.

events.title: Tokyo breaks for lunch
events.description: A good checkpoint to see whether Asia's opening move has deepened or faded.

events.title: NSE pre-open begins
events.description: Orders are collected until 9:08 am and matched in the call auction to set opening prices.

events.title: NSE and BSE open
events.description: Continuous trading begins, with the global picture already priced into the open.

markDefs.definition: NSE's volatility index, calculated from Nifty 50 option prices. It shows how much movement traders expect over the next 30 days. A rising India VIX signals rising fear.

Futures contracts on indices such as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 that trade almost 23 hours a day on CME. They show how US markets are moving during the Indian morning, long after the US cash market has closed.

children.text: You do not need 50 screens. These ten numbers capture every link in the chain from Lesson 2: the global trigger, the dollar, foreign money, the rupee, Asia's reaction and India's own fear gauge. Two of them deserve special mention.

Oil marketing companies, paints, airlines, the rupee

body.text: Add an eleventh item on results days: overnight company news. If an Indian company with a US listing, such as Infosys (INFY) or HDFC Bank (HDB), reported results after NSE closed, its ADR's move in New York is your best early guide to how the stock may open.

markDefs.definition: The normal gap between a futures price and the underlying index, reflecting interest costs until expiry minus expected dividends. Nifty futures, including GIFT Nifty, usually trade at a premium to the spot Nifty for this reason.

children.text: The most common mistake is comparing GIFT Nifty directly with the previous Nifty close. GIFT Nifty is a futures contract, so it normally trades above the spot index because of the

. A GIFT Nifty level 40 points above yesterday's close can actually signal a flat or slightly weaker open if the usual premium is 60 points. Watch the change in the gap, not just the headline level. The premium varies with interest rates and the number of days to expiry, so compare today's gap with its recent normal level.

body.latex: \text{Implied Nifty open} \approx \text{GIFT Nifty} - \text{Normal premium} \qquad \text{Implied gap (\%)} = \left(\frac{\text{Implied open}}{\text{Previous Nifty close}} - 1\right) \times 100
body.caption: Adjust GIFT Nifty for its normal futures premium before estimating the Nifty's open

body.title: Estimate the opening gap
body.prompt: Illustrative figures: the Nifty 50 closed at 23,118.60. At 7:45 am IST, GIFT Nifty is trading at 23,050, and over recent days it has typically traded about 60 points above the spot Nifty. What opening gap does this imply, in percent? Enter a negative number for a lower open, rounded to two decimal places.
body.explanation: Implied open ≈ 23,050 − 60 = 22,990. Implied gap = (22,990 ÷ 23,118.60 − 1) × 100 = (0.99444 − 1) × 100 = −0.56%. If you had compared 23,050 directly with 23,118.60, you would have estimated a −0.30% open and underestimated the fall by almost half. Treat the result as a rough guide: the actual open is set by the NSE pre-open auction.

body.text: GIFT Nifty is a guide, not a guarantee. Liquidity is thinner early in the morning, news can break between 7:00 am and 9:15 am, and the premium shifts as expiry approaches. Use it to set expectations, and let the NSE pre-open auction at 9:00 am confirm them.

children.text: Turn the Numbers Into a Simple Score

Ten numbers can still feel overwhelming. A quick way to summarise them is a risk score: give each indicator +1 if it points to risk-on, −1 if it points to risk-off and 0 if it is neutral, then add them up. A strongly negative score warns of a difficult session and a strongly positive one of a supportive session. It is a way to organise your thinking, not a trading signal.

body.title: Score the morning
body.prompt: Using the illustrative snapshot, score each indicator +1 for risk-on, −1 for risk-off and 0 for neutral. What is the total score?
body.explanation: Risk-on (+1 each): S&P 500 up, Brent down, Nikkei and KOSPI up. That is +3. Neutral (0): flat US futures. Risk-off (−1 each): rising US yields, a stronger dollar, GIFT Nifty implying a lower open, a weaker rupee, FPI selling and a rising India VIX. That is −6. Total = +3 − 6 = −3. Even though Wall Street and Asia were up, the India-specific links, including yields, the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows, point to a cautious open. Global good news does not always translate into Indian good news.

children.text: The Global Economic Calendar in IST

Your morning dashboard tells you what already happened. An economic calendar tells you what is coming. Knowing when big announcements land in Indian time helps you avoid being surprised, and helps you understand why markets sometimes go quiet before a major event.

body.caption: Key recurring market events in IST (US and Europe on daylight saving time; add one hour in winter)

cells: Usually late morning Tokyo time, roughly 8:00 am to 9:30 am
Banks, NBFCs, realty, autos and the rupee
RBI rate expectations and bond yields
US yields, the dollar and FPI flows
Fed expectations and global risk appetite
The single biggest global driver of FPI flows

body.title: India's own big event
body.textWithBlank: The RBI Governor announces the Monetary Policy Committee's decision at ___ am IST, while NSE is already trading.
body.explanation: RBI policy decisions are announced at 10:00 am IST, during market hours, so Indian stocks react in real time. That is very different from Fed, ECB and US data announcements, which arrive after NSE has closed and show up in the next morning's gap opening.

children.text: What the Dashboard Is For, and What It Is Not

columns.label: Use it to
points: Understand why the market is moving before you react
Separate global shocks from problems with Indian companies
Avoid placing large market orders into an obvious gap-down open
Spot which sectors are likely to lead or lag today
Stay calm, and keep your SIPs running through global volatility

columns.label: Do not use it to
points: Trade every morning based on a single score
Assume GIFT Nifty guarantees the opening level
Abandon long-term plans because of one night's news
Chase F&O trades, where SEBI found 93% of individual traders lost money over FY22 to FY24
Replace research on the businesses you actually own

body.title: Build your morning plan
body.scenario: It is 7:45 am IST. Overnight, the S&P 500 fell 1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.6%. The US 10-year yield is up to 5.08%, the dollar index is stronger and Brent crude is above $109. The Nikkei and KOSPI are down about 1.5%. GIFT Nifty implies a 0.9% lower open. Yesterday the rupee closed weaker and FPIs were net sellers, while DIIs were net buyers. India VIX rose. A major US Federal Reserve decision is due tonight at 11:30 pm IST. You are a long-term investor with a monthly SIP, and you had planned to buy ₹50,000 worth of a large private bank's shares this morning.
body.prompt: Score this morning, explain what it tells you, and decide what you will do about your SIP and your planned bank stock purchase.
body.modelAnswer:
Score: Nearly every indicator is risk-off: US stocks down, higher yields, a stronger dollar, higher oil, weaker Asia, GIFT Nifty implying a lower open, a weaker rupee, FPI selling and rising India VIX. DII buying is the only cushion. A score of around −9 signals a clearly difficult session.

What it tells you: This is a global, rate-and-oil-driven sell-off, not news about Indian banks. Private banks are FPI favourites and rate-sensitive, so they may fall more than the index today. The Fed decision tonight adds uncertainty, so volatility may stay high for another session.

SIP: Keep it running. SIPs are designed for exactly these days, when the same monthly amount buys more units.

Planned bank purchase: As a long-term investor, you do not need to buy in the first minutes of a gap-down open. Sensible options include waiting until after the opening volatility settles, using a limit order at a price you are comfortable with, splitting the purchase into two or three parts across the next few sessions, or waiting until after the Fed decision. What should not change is your view of the bank itself, which should be based on its business, not one morning's dashboard.

body.title: Your 15-minute global morning routine
steps: Minute 1 to 3: Check the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and US futures, and note any big overnight company results, including Indian ADRs.
Minute 4 to 6: Check the US 10-year yield, the US Dollar Index and Brent crude.
Minute 7 to 9: Check the Nikkei, KOSPI, TAIEX and Hang Seng.
Minute 10 to 12: Check GIFT Nifty, adjust for its normal premium and estimate the opening gap.
Minute 13 to 15: Check yesterday's USD/INR close, FPI and DII flows and India VIX, look at today's economic calendar, and write down your risk score.

body.description: Pre-open market data, India VIX, provisional FII and DII activity, and live Nifty levels.

body.label: Investing.com Economic Calendar
body.description: A global calendar of data releases and central bank decisions that you can set to Indian Standard Time.

cards.definition: NSE's volatility index, based on Nifty 50 option prices. A rising India VIX signals rising fear and expected volatility.
Near round-the-clock futures on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 that show the US mood during the Indian morning.
The normal premium of a futures price over the spot index, which must be adjusted for when reading GIFT Nifty.
(GIFT Nifty − normal premium) ÷ previous Nifty close − 1, a rough estimate of where the Nifty may open.
A market mood in which investors buy riskier assets such as emerging market shares, usually with falling yields, a softer dollar and steady oil.
A market mood in which investors sell riskier assets and seek safety, usually with rising yields, a stronger dollar and FPI selling from India.
A schedule of upcoming data releases and central bank decisions, used to anticipate market-moving events.

points: Run your global check between about 7:30 am and 8:30 am IST, when most of Asia is trading and GIFT Nifty is active.
Ten numbers cover the whole transmission chain: US closes, US futures, US 10-year yield, the dollar index, Brent, Asian indices, GIFT Nifty, USD/INR, FPI and DII flows, and India VIX.
Always adjust GIFT Nifty for its normal futures premium before estimating the Nifty's open.
A simple +1, 0 or −1 score for each indicator turns the dashboard into a quick read of risk-on or risk-off conditions.
Use an economic calendar in IST: RBI decisions land at 10:00 am during trading, while US data and Fed decisions arrive in the Indian evening and night.
The dashboard is for context and calm decisions, not for daily trading. Keep SIPs running and base stock decisions on the businesses you own.

body.text: That completes the course. You started by learning why India is a 3% slice of a global market dominated by the US. You explored how Wall Street, Europe's exchanges, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Korea and Singapore work, compared their valuations and growth, and traced how their money, currencies and time zones move the Nifty. The next time the Nifty opens sharply lower for no obvious Indian reason, you will know where to look, and you will already have looked.

This lesson is for education only and is not investment or trading advice. Market figures for 15 September 2026 are drawn from NSE and published reports. Event timings are typical and can change, especially when daylight saving time shifts. GIFT Nifty premiums, dashboard readings and risk scores in the exercises are illustrative. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any security.
